title: Hanuman's first words
hook: a stranger's sentence so well made that Rama names every virtue in it

segments.voice: Yesterday: Hanuman walked down the mountain disguised as a bhikshu, a wandering mendicant. Same costume, opposite hearts. Today the week closes.

Have you ever met someone and known within a minute, from how they spoke, that you could trust them? Not from what they said, exactly. From how. Hanuman reaches the brothers and speaks, and when he's finished, Rama turns to Lakshmana and says something remarkable about a stranger's sentence. Remember where Rama is. He has lost his kingdom, his father and now his wife. He has no reason to trust anyone on this mountain. And a few sentences from a stranger change that.
screen: `NOT WHAT, BUT HOW.` → `RAMA TURNS TO LAKSHMANA.`

segments.voice: Hanuman greets them with respect. You look like sages, he says, or like kings: why are you in this forest? Then he tells them who he is: a minister of Sugriva, a monkey king driven out by his brother, who wants their friendship. He's careful and warm, and honest about who sent him. Then Rama turns to Lakshmana, and his praise is precise. Nobody could speak like this, he says, who hadn't learned the Rig Veda, the Yajur Veda and the Sama Veda. He has clearly studied grammar well; in all he said, not one word was wrong. Nothing in his face, his eyes or his brow was out of place. He didn't drag it out or rush it. His voice came from the chest and throat, in a middle pitch, clear and pleasing. A king with a messenger like this, Rama says, can get anything done. Notice what Rama praises: not strength, but speech. Good speech here is a kind of goodness, right in length, right in tone, honest about who sent him. And Rama, grieving and exhausted, still notices a stranger's care with words, and says so. Now the week, from the top. Jatayu's last breath and his funeral. Kabandha, and the curse that came from a prank. Shabari, waiting, and the flowers that never withered. Lake Pampa in spring. And today, a sentence that starts a friendship.
screen: `A MINISTER OF SUGRIVA.` · `NOT ONE WORD WRONG.` · `NOT TOO LONG, NOT RUSHED.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `A SENTENCE THAT STARTS A FRIENDSHIP.`

segments.voice: Choose one true, kind sentence you might say to someone soon, and say it silently once. Then shape it, a word too many, a tone not quite right, and say it again in your head a little cleaner, until it rests easy.
Vakya, a sentence: what Rama praises when Hanuman speaks, saying no word was wrong, not too long, not rushed.
Your line: not one word wrong. Rama heard a friend in the way a stranger spoke. That's day five hundred eighty-one.

howItsDone: Devotees honor Hanuman for learning and eloquence as well as strength, and this passage, where Rama praises his grammar and delivery, is one source of that picture.
